correctness.rationale: The proof is an infinite arithmetic reduction, not enumeration: Pell-associated-Pell identities give 2 S_n=B_k Q_{4n+2k}-k and S_{n+1}-S_n=4 B_k P_{4n+2k+2}. Strong divisibility of Pell P yields gcd_n P_{4n+2k+2}=2 for even k and 12 for odd k. Consequently H(k)=gcd((B_k Q_{2k}-k)/2,8B_k) or gcd((B_k Q_{2k}-k)/2,48B_k). For odd primes other than 3, valuations agree with gcd(B_k,k); for odd multiples of 3, B_k is a 3-unit and Q_{2k} divisible by 3 so exactly one extra 3 occurs. The two-adic duplication and unit mod4 arguments give v2(H)=v2(gcd(B_k,k)) for all k. Independent integer generation of 35 windows for k=1..24 reproduced the proposed gcd, but finite windows are corroboration only. No extra assumptions on k or n.
residual_risks: A later or unindexed solution to the original published Question 30 may exist; originality is best-of-knowledge.
The proof is for squared Lucas-cobalancing windows; not the unsolved squared cobalancing or higher powers.
Finite k/windows do not establish the all-k formula.

originality.rationale: The original published 2023 Article 23.6.4 explicitly lists the squared Lucas-cobalancing window problem as Question 30 with numerical 3x anomaly at odd multiples of 3; its Partial Result 29 treats squared Pell/associated Pell, and Question 31 leaves gcd(B_k,k) structural study separately open. These facts are not a theorem of the submitted expression and require the nontrivial odd-index associated-Pell reduction and exceptional valuations. Resultary searches returned other Lucas/Pell arithmetic without this statement. No covering theorem found among material read; unindexed related solutions are possible.

value.rationale: An explicit named open problem for a standard recurrence family receives a uniform, all-k exact gcd and proof of the exceptional factor. The invariant and exceptional congruence class were independently motivated by the source; it is not a small-index recomputation. The remaining gcd(B_k,k) factor is correctly outside claim.
